title: Lifetime, Shadowing, and Closure Intuition
definition: Lifetime describes when state exists or remains reachable; shadowing makes a nearer same-named binding win during lookup, and a closure can preserve access to an enclosing binding after the enclosing call returns.
purpose: Separate name visibility from state existence and explain surprising nested-function behavior.
history: Languages implement storage duration and closure capture differently, so curriculum claims must separate the general model from JavaScript behavior.
mental_model: A name is a route on a map, while lifetime is how long the destination remains available; a closure can retain a route beyond the original call.
analogy: Two employees may share a name, and an archived contact may remain reachable after a meeting; the analogy does not model automatic memory management.
common_mistakes: Equating end of scope with immediate memory reclamation
Assuming closure captures a frozen copy
industry_notes: Lifetime bugs often appear as stale state, unexpected retention, or callbacks observing later mutations.
ai_notes: Demand a time-ordered trace and distinguish binding, value, and reachable object.
interview_notes: Ask how a returned function can still read an enclosing variable.
